purpose: Reproducible public-source evidence for the Jammy default CA-file path mismatch; no package code execution.

public_runtime_observation.meaning: The v10 helper reached the CA-file predicate after successful imports and Python/APT version predicates.
limits: No observation establishes whether /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt was generated.
No observation independently establishes the actual loaded libcrypto bytes or its default path in the failed process.
The source/package mismatch is proven for the exact public archives inspected; this is not a claim that the missing default alias is the only hosted defect.

verification_performed: InRelease SHA256 matches the frozen bootstrap anchor.
Packages.xz byte count and SHA256 match the InRelease SHA256 entry.
Inspected binary package byte counts and SHA256 values match their exact index stanzas.
metadata_chain.signature_limit: No independent signature-verification claim is made by this artifact. The frozen bootstrap separately verifies InRelease signatures. A local research recheck was unavailable because gpgv was not installed; no installation was attempted.

ubuntu_source_packaging.authentication_limit: The Debian tar checksum matches the official HTTPS-retrieved .dsc. The .dsc signature was not independently verified and this source archive was not anchored through a signed Sources index in this research.

source_locations.finding: Move certs, openssl.cnf and private to /etc/ssl and create links for only those names.
Install manifest names certs, private, misc and openssl.cnf under usr/lib/ssl; no cert.pem.
Creates /usr/lib/ssl -> /etc/ssl only if /usr/lib/ssl does not exist; does not create cert.pem.

control_members.finding: Runs update-ca-certificates during configuration and for registered update triggers.

locations.finding: Selected certificate data is appended by add() to the temporary bundle.
The temporary bundle is installed only if it exists; no /usr/lib/ssl/cert.pem alias is created.

primary_api_sources.finding: Calls X509_get_default_cert_file_env() and X509_get_default_cert_file() to obtain file defaults.
cafile is None if the resolved file does not exist.
Default CAfile and CApath are separate; SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR can override them. A missing default location need not make set_default_verify_paths fail.
Ubuntu generates the combined bundle as /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt.
